A compact view of a roadmap's page: prototypes

Static frames of a roadmap's page on a desktop (1280px wide, the navigation open) and a phone (375px), all drawn from one sample roadmap: Appointment booking, with 18 items and 3 unpublished changes, on 18 November 2026. Journey 1 sets three compact views beside today's cards. Journey 2 sets out three places for the switch between cards and compact.

Nothing here works. Each frame's label names its moment and where keyboard focus is. The analysis beside this page, roadmap-compact-view-ux-analysis.md, compares the designs and lists the decisions.

1. Read and work a roadmap in a compact view

Sam Evans opens Appointment booking to check the plan and move an item. As cards its 18 items run to about eight screens on a desktop and twelve on a phone. Each design is what the page shows once Compact is chosen: the same header, placements, pending marks and foot bar, with the items drawn smaller.

Each compact design starts with the whole page, then the screen once scrolled to Now, then that screen with an item opened or a menu open. Journey 1 draws the switch where design D of journey 2 puts it.

2. Switch between cards and compact

Where the switch sits and what it is. Every frame draws design A's rows as the compact view; the question is the same for B and C.
